title: Mortal Kombat 11
summary: Has the face morph read its three-float deltas the way D3DMetal and DXMT can, which removes the dark patches, and gives the movies their colours and their frame order back. DirectX 12 and 11 alike.

credits.name: Anton Pavliuk
credits.note: Found and published first that the movie frames come out in decode order, and the reordering (MIT, DirectX 11 only); mk11-movie.c is a separate implementation.

excerpts.note: The faces. Every three-float buffer view is created as a one-float view three times as long, which D3DMetal and DXMT both read correctly; the rewritten morph shaders then read a delta's three floats one by one.
The colours. CrossOver's H.264 decoder leaves NV12 out of the types it offers, so the game took YV12 and drew it as NV12. NV12 is offered again, first.
The frame order. The decoder hands frames out in decode order; the fix holds them and hands out the one that comes first in display order.
